title: Use the real file API and walk a directory tree
brief: Read and write files with raw file descriptors, inspect inodes, tell hard links from symbolic links, print a directory tree, and normalise paths.
hints: os.write may write fewer bytes than you asked for. Loop, slicing off what was written, until nothing is left. Always close the descriptor in a finally block.
os.read(fd, n) returns b'' at end of file. Read in chunks of 4096 or so and join the pieces.
os.stat follows symbolic links and os.lstat does not. A hard link shares both st_dev and st_ino with the original. A symbolic link has its own inode.
For walk_tree, sort the os.scandir entries by name, use entry.is_dir(follow_symlinks=False), and call os.readlink for symbolic links. Recurse with depth + 1.

For normalize_path, split on '/', skip empty parts and '.', and keep a stack. A '..' pops the stack, unless the stack is empty: then an absolute path drops it and a relative path keeps it. Also keep it when the top of the stack is itself a '..'.
